en: to become tasteless; to get stale

examples.en: The cola has gone flat, so it doesn't taste good.
I don't want to drink flat soda.
I left the lid open and it went flat.
The story ended in an anticlimax and I was disappointed.
I sang a song so that the mood wouldn't go flat.

examples.ko: 김빠질까 봐 탄산음료는 뚜껑을 꼭 닫아요.
examples.en: I close fizzy drinks tightly so they don't go flat.

explain: '김이 빠지다'가 줄어든 말이고, 탄산음료의 기포가 없어질 때와 재미나 흥이 없어질 때 모두 써요. 비슷한 '김새다'는 기대나 흥이 갑자기 꺾일 때 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a contracted form of '김이 빠지다' and is used both when a fizzy drink loses its bubbles and when the fun or excitement fades. The similar '김새다' is used more often when expectations or excitement suddenly get deflated.

en: late summer heat; lingering summer heat

examples.en: Even though it's September, the lingering summer heat continues.

examples.ko: 올해는 늦더위 때문에 가을옷을 못 입었어요.
examples.en: This year I couldn't wear autumn clothes because of the late heat.
The late heat is severe, so I still turn on the air conditioner.
They say the lingering heat will ease from tomorrow.
I'm worn out by the late heat and have no appetite.
Even after Chuseok, the late heat hasn't gone away.

explain: 여름이 지났는데도 남아 있는 더위를 말해요. 뉴스나 날씨 이야기에서 '늦더위가 기승을 부리다', '늦더위가 이어지다'로 자주 나와요. 반대로 봄에 늦게까지 남은 추위는 '늦추위'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means heat that remains after summer should be over. In news and weather talk you see '늦더위가 기승을 부리다' and '늦더위가 이어지다'. The cold that lingers into spring is '늦추위'.

examples.en: It was so cold that my teeth chattered.
The sound of shoes clicked down the hallway.

examples.ko: 아이가 딱딱 소리가 나게 손뼉을 쳤어요.
examples.en: The child clapped with sharp clacks.
I heard the ice cracking.
I lined the papers up neatly and filed them.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 일을 딱딱 처리해서 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: That employee gets things done crisply, so I trust him.

explain: 딱딱은 단단한 것이 부딪치거나 갈라지는 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. 일이 빠르고 정확하게 맞아떨어질 때 '딱딱 맞다', '딱딱 처리하다'처럼도 써요. 모양이 비슷한 '딱딱하다'는 '단단하다, 굳었다'는 형용사라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: 딱딱 imitates the sound of hard things clicking or cracking. It also describes things that go quickly and precisely, as in '딱딱 맞다' or '딱딱 처리하다'. The similar-looking adjective '딱딱하다' means hard or stiff, which is a different word.

examples.en: The rice is undercooked and hard to eat.
The potatoes weren't cooked enough, so they were underdone.
Half-ripe fruit tastes underdone.
If the meat is undercooked, I'll grill it again.
The noodles are fine even if they're a bit underdone.
I cooked the undercooked rice again.

explain: 음식이 덜 익은 상태를 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '덜 익다'도 쓰는데, '설다'는 주로 밥이나 과일에 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이라 '선 밥'처럼 변해요. '설익다'는 비슷하지만 따로 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: Describes food that isn't fully cooked. '덜 익다' means the same, but '설다' is mostly for rice and fruit. The ㄹ stem changes as in '선 밥'. '설익다' is a similar but separate word.

examples.en: When I was little, I often played house.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난하듯 가게를 차렸다가 금방 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: They opened a shop as if playing house and soon closed it.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난 같은 연애는 이제 그만하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to stop dating that's like a childish game.
The child sets a table with toy play dishes.
This isn't child's play, it's a real job.

examples.ko: 소꿉장난 속 아빠 역할은 늘 제가 했어요.
examples.en: In our house-playing game, I always played the dad.

explain: 아이들이 소꿉으로 집안일을 흉내 내며 노는 것이에요. 어릴 때부터 함께 놀던 친구는 '소꿉친구'라고 해요. 어른의 일이 어설프고 진지하지 않을 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 회사 일을 소꿉장난처럼 하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't treat work at a company like child's play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 진지하지 않고 어설프게 할 때 비판하듯 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when someone does something in a non-serious, amateurish way.

explain_en: It is the children's game of imitating housework with toy kitchenware. A friend you have known since playing together as a child is a '소꿉친구'. It is also used figuratively when an adult's work is clumsy and not serious.

examples.ko: 이 조사 결과는 신뢰성이 높지 않아요.
examples.en: The reliability of this survey result is not high.
Please find reliable materials.
I'm worried about whether the reviews can be trusted.
To boost credibility, you need to state your sources.
You need a habit of checking how reliable the news is.
This product passed a reliability test.

explain: '신뢰'는 사람이나 조직에 대한 믿음에도 쓰지만, '신뢰성'은 정보, 자료, 제품이 믿을 만한 정도를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '신뢰성이 높다/낮다/있다/없다'처럼 써요. 대화에서는 '믿을 만하다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: '신뢰' can be trust in people or organizations, but '신뢰성' fits how trustworthy information, data or products are. Use it as '신뢰성이 높다/낮다/있다/없다'. In casual talk, '믿을 만하다' is easier.

examples.en: Our team conceded no points in the first half.
Defense is important to concede fewer points.
The players wobbled after the first goal against.

examples.ko: 그 투수는 한 경기 평균 실점이 낮아요.
examples.en: That pitcher gives up few runs per game on average.
We conceded only once, but the result was a loss.
The goalkeeper's mistake led to a goal against.

explain: '실점'은 경기에서 상대에게 점수를 내주는 거예요. 짝말은 '득점'이에요. '실점을 하다/줄이다/막다'처럼 써요. 시험에서 점수가 깎이는 건 '감점'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '실점' is giving up a point to the opponent in a game, and its pair is '득점' (scoring). It goes with '하다', '줄이다' and '막다'. Losing marks on a test is '감점'.

examples.en: An error came up as soon as I opened the app.
I took a photo of the error message and sent it.
I keep getting errors when I log in.
The error went away when I restarted the app.
The screen froze because of an error during payment.
Even the same error looks different on each computer.

explain: 컴퓨터나 앱에 문제가 생겼을 때 '에러가 나다', '에러가 뜨다'라고 말해요. 같은 뜻의 한자어 '오류'도 있고, '오류가 뜨다'처럼 같은 동사와 어울려요.
explain_en: When a computer or app has a problem, you say 에러가 나다 or 에러가 뜨다. The Sino-Korean word 오류 means the same and takes the same verbs, as in 오류가 뜨다.

examples.ko: 아이들 옷은 원색이 많아서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: Children's clothes have lots of primary colors, so they stand out.

examples.ko: 원색 포스터는 멀리서도 눈에 잘 보여요.
examples.en: Brightly colored posters are easy to see even from far away.
I feel more comfortable with soft colors than with vivid ones.

examples.ko: 원색으로 칠한 벽 때문에 방이 화려해 보여요.
examples.en: The walls painted in bold colors make the room look flashy.

examples.ko: 한복은 원색을 많이 써서 아주 화려해요.
examples.en: Hanbok uses many vivid colors, so it is very colorful.
Red, blue, and yellow are typical primary colors.

explain: '원색'은 선명하고 강한 느낌이라 '화려하다', '눈에 띄다'와 같이 자주 나와요. 반대로 '파스텔 톤', '연한 색', '무채색'은 부드럽거나 차분한 느낌이에요. 아래 '원색적이다'는 색이 아니라 말과 표현에 쓰는 별도 쓰임이에요.

phrases.example: 그 비판은 너무 원색적이어서 듣기 불편했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 표현이 꾸밈없이 거칠고 직접적일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or expressions are rough, unfiltered, and direct.

explain_en: '원색' has a vivid, strong feel and often appears with '화려하다' and '눈에 띄다'. By contrast, '파스텔 톤', '연한 색', and '무채색' feel soft or calm. '원색적이다' below is a separate use for words and expressions, not colors.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 항상 재미있는 조크를 해요.
examples.en: That person always tells funny jokes.

examples.ko: 조크가 너무 썰렁해서 아무도 웃지 않았어요.
examples.en: The joke was so lame that nobody laughed.

examples.ko: 회의 분위기를 풀려고 가벼운 조크로 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started with a light joke to ease the meeting mood.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구가 영어 조크를 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: A foreign friend explained an English joke to me.
I thought it was a joke, but it was real.
The staff laughed at the boss's joke.

explain: '농담'이 훨씬 자연스럽고 흔해요. 조크는 영어 joke에서 온 말이라 가볍고 약간 영어식인 느낌이 있어요. 진짜로 하는 말은 '진담'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 농담 is far more natural and common. 조크 comes from English 'joke' and feels light and slightly English-flavored. What you say seriously is 진담.

en: dash; speeding; running at full speed

examples.en: I heard the sound of motorcycles speeding all night.
The athlete's final dash was really cool.
Reckless speeding leads to accidents.

examples.ko: 그 경주마는 초원에서 힘차게 질주를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The racehorse began a powerful gallop across the grassland.
Speeding on the road at night is dangerous.
I made one last dash just before the finish line.

explain: '질주'는 아주 빠르게 달리는 모습을 말해요. 달리기보다 자동차, 오토바이, 말처럼 속도가 큰 것에 어울려요. 도로에서는 위험하다는 느낌도 있어서 '난폭 질주'처럼 나쁜 뜻으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 질주 describes running or driving at a great speed, and fits cars, motorcycles and horses more than ordinary jogging. On roads it carries a sense of danger, as in '난폭 질주' (reckless speeding).
